62324-grifters-asteroid.creator: Unknown
62324-grifters-asteroid.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Without a word, the bartender reached under the counter, brought out two glasses of water. The interplanetary con-men drank noisily, asked for more, until they had drunk eight glasses. Meanwhile, the bartender had taken out eight jiggers and filled them with whiskey.

arxiv-1405-0628.title: Infinite-State Energy Games Thanks: This is the technical report number EDI-INF-RR-1419 of the School of Informatics at the University of Edinburgh, UK. (http://www.inf.ed.ac.uk/publications/report/). Full version (including proofs) of material presented at CSL-LICS 2014 (Vienna, Austria). arXiv.org
arxiv-1405-0628.creator: Parosh Aziz Abdulla 1 , Mohamed Faouzi Atig 1 , Piotr Hofman 2 , Richard Mayr 4 , K. Narayan Kumar 3 , Patrick Totzke 4
arxiv-1405-0628.description: Abstract Energy games are a well-studied class of 2-player turn-based games on a finite graph where transitions are labeled with integer vectors which represent changes in a multidimensional resource (the energy). One player tries to keep the cumulative changes non-negative in every component while the other tries to frustrate this.

arxiv-2210-12949.title: Enhancing Label Consistency on Document-level Named Entity Recognition
arxiv-2210-12949.creator: Minbyul Jeong \sfb 1 and Jaewoo Kang \sfb 1,2,3,*
arxiv-2210-12949.description: Abstract Summary: Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental part of extracting information from documents in biomedical applications. A notable advantage of NER is its consistency in extracting biomedical entities in a document context. Although existing document NER models show consistent predictions, they still do not meet our expectations.

arxiv-2307-14270.title: Socioeconomic agents as active matter in nonequilibrium Sakoda-Schelling models
arxiv-2307-14270.creator: Ruben Zakine, Jérôme Garnier-Brun, Antoine-Cyrus Becharat, Michael Benzaquen
arxiv-2307-14270.description: Abstract How robust are socioeconomic agent-based models with respect to the details of the agents’ decision rule? We tackle this question by considering an occupation model in the spirit of the Sakoda-Schelling model, historically introduced to shed light on segregation dynamics among human groups.

arxiv-2407-04508.title: Layer-Dependent Charge State Lifetime of Single Se Vacancies in WSe 2 \text{WSe}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\vphantom{\text{2}}\smash[t]{\text{2}}}^{\vphantom{\smash[t]{\text{2}}}\hphantom{\text{2}}\text{}}
arxiv-2407-04508.creator: Laric Bobzien †, Jonas Allerbeck †, Nils Krane, Andres Ortega-Guerrero, Zihao Wang, Daniel E. Cintron Figueroa, Chengye Dong, Carlo A. Pignedoli, Joshua A. Robinson, Bruno Schuler
arxiv-2407-04508.description: Abstract Defect engineering in two-dimensional semiconductors has been exploited to tune the optoelectronic properties and introduce new quantum states in the band gap. Chalcogen vacancies in transition metal dichalcogenides in particular have been found to strongly impact charge carrier concentration and mobility in 2D transistors as well as feature sub-gap emission and single-photon response.

arxiv-2506-13579.title: Flexible-length Text Infilling for Discrete Diffusion Models
arxiv-2506-13579.creator: Andrew Zhang, Anushka Sivakumar, Chiawei Tang, Chris Thomas
arxiv-2506-13579.description: Abstract Discrete diffusion models are a new class of text generators that offer advantages such as bidirectional context use, parallelizable generation, and flexible prompting compared to autoregressive models. However, a critical limitation of discrete diffusion models is their inability to perform flexible-length or flexible-position text infilling without access to ground-truth positional data.

arxiv-2508-19306.title: A Goal-Driven Ruin and Recreate Heuristic for the 2D Variable-Sized Bin Packing Problem with Guillotine Constraints Journal: European Journal of Operational Research
arxiv-2508-19306.creator: Jeroen Gardeyn, Tony Wauters
arxiv-2508-19306.description: Abstract This paper addresses the two-dimensional bin packing problem with guillotine constraints. The problem requires a set of rectangular items to be cut from larger rectangles, known as bins, while only making use of edge-to-edge (guillotine) cuts. The goal is to minimize the total bin area needed to cut all required items.

arxiv-2509-03403.title: Beyond Correctness: Harmonizing Process and Outcome Rewards through RL Training
arxiv-2509-03403.creator: Chenlu Ye, Zhou Yu, Ziji Zhang, Hao Chen, Narayanan Sadagopan, Jing Huang, Tong Zhang, Anurag Beniwal
arxiv-2509-03403.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged to be a predominant paradigm for mathematical reasoning tasks, offering stable improvements in reasoning ability. However, Outcome Reward Models (ORMs) in RLVR are too coarse-grained to distinguish flawed reasoning within correct answers or valid reasoning within incorrect answers.

arxiv-2510-01704.title: Holistic Order Prediction in Natural Scenes
arxiv-2510-01704.creator: Pierre Musacchio, Hyunmin Lee, Jaesik Park
arxiv-2510-01704.description: Abstract Even in controlled settings, understanding instance-wise geometries is a challenging task for a wide range of visual models. Although specialized systems exist, modern arts rely on expensive input formats (category labels, binary segmentation masks) and inference costs (a quadratic amount of forward passes). We mitigate these limitations by proposing InstaFormer , a network capable of holistic order prediction .

arxiv-2511-00867.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Conflict Occurrence and Fatalities in Ethiopia: A Bayesian Model and Predictive Insights Using Event-level Data (1997 – 2024)
arxiv-2511-00867.creator: Yassin Tesfaw Abebe, Abdu Mohammed Seid, Lassi Roininen, Mohammed Seid Ali
arxiv-2511-00867.description: Abstract This study presents a spatiotemporal, dual Bayesian model designed to examine both the occurrence and the number of conflict fatalities using event-level data applied to over 28 years of conflict data from Ethiopia spanning 1997–2024, sourced from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) project.

Following our recent study on vaccine penetration by targeting of vaccine to human hair follicular

pmc-10601164.title: Longitudinal changes of oxidative stress and PON1 lactonase activity and status in older pregnant women undergoing assisted reproductive technology: a prospective nested case-control study
pmc-10601164.creator: Chenyu Jiang, Meng Chen, Yujie Wu, Huai Bai, Xinghui Liu, Ping Fan
pmc-10601164.description: BackgroundChildbearing in women with advanced maternal age (AMA) has increased the need for artificial reproductive technology (ART). ART and oxidative stress are associated with many pregnancy complications. Paraoxonase (PON) 1 is one of the key components responsible for antioxidative activity in high-density lipoprotein (HDL).

pmc-10750583.title: Immediate Weight Bearing after Modified-Brostrom Reconstruction: A Retrospective Review of an Accelerated Rehab Protocol
pmc-10750583.creator: Christian Curatolo, Andrew Robert Rust, Kevin D Martin, Harish Chinnasamy
pmc-10750583.description: Category:Ankle; SportsIntroduction/Purpose:Majority of injuries to the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) will go on to heal with non-operative management. Nearly a third of these injuries, however, will go on to develop chronic pain and instability; in these cases, operative reconstruction is indicated. An anatomic modified Broström reconstruction has replaced a traditional tenodesis as the standard of care.

pmc-11440546.title: Nuclear Quantum Effects on the Nature of Hydroboration Selectivity: Experimental Effects of First-Collision Tunneling
pmc-11440546.creator: Christoph
pmc-11440546.description: The understanding of selectivity in reactions exhibiting nonstatistical dynamics is impeded by the limitations of trajectory studies with regard to nuclear quantum effects, especially tunneling. We described here the use of ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) to account for an unusual regiochemical isotope effect on the regioselectivity of hydroborations of alkenes with BH3/BD3.

pmc-11700529.title: Remarkable Response to Dabrafenib and Trametinib in a V-Raf Murine Sarcoma Viral Oncogene Homolog B (BRAF) V600E-Mutated Lung Adenocarcinoma Patient With Poor Performance Status and Respiratory Failure: A Case Report
pmc-11700529.creator: Satoshi Anai, Kohei Isa, Rin Chibana, Shiho Ueno, Yoko Sato
pmc-11700529.description: We report the case of a 73-year-old man with progressive dyspnea and acute respiratory failure. Imaging revealed extensive infiltrative shadows in the right lung. A bronchoscopic biopsy confirmed primary lung adenocarcinoma harboring the BRAF V600E mutation. The patient's performance score was three, requiring four liter/minute of supplemental oxygen to maintain an oxygen saturation of 90%.

pmc-12352165.title: Fabrication of 3D Printed, Core‐and‐Shell Implants as Controlled Release Systems for Local siRNA Delivery
pmc-12352165.creator: Dina B. Mahmoud, Christian Wölk, Michaela Schulz‐Siegmund
pmc-12352165.description: The development and clinical translation of small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapies remains challenging owing to their poor pharmacokinetics. 3D printing technology presents a great opportunity to fabricate personalized implants for local and sustained delivery of siRNA. Hydrogels can mimic the mechanical properties of tissues, avoiding the problems associated with rigid implants.

pmc-12373968.title: Development of data driven models to accurately estimate density of fatty acid ethyl esters
pmc-12373968.creator: Walid Abdelfattah, Munthar Kadhim Abosaoda, Hardik Doshi, H. S. Shreenidhi, Manoranjan Parhi, Devendra Singh, Prabhjot Singh, Abdolali Yarahmadi Kandahari
pmc-12373968.description: Fatty acid ethyl esters (FAEEs) are widely used in biofuels, pharmaceuticals, and lubricants, offering an eco-friendly alternative due to their biodegradability and renewable nature, contributing to environmental sustainability. The objective of this study is to construct advanced predictive algorithms using various machine learning methods, including AdaBoost, Decision Trees, KNN, Random Forests, Ensemble Learning, CNN, and SVR.

pmc-12439691.title: Impact of Intraoperative Postural Transitions on Internal Carotid Artery Blood Flow During Gynecologic Laparoscopic Surgery
pmc-12439691.creator: Xi Tan, Wenyi Sun, Hao Zhou, Li Zhang, Chaoxuan Dong
pmc-12439691.description: ObjectiveReduced internal carotid artery (ICA) blood flow can cause cerebral hypoperfusion, increasing the risk of intraoperative or postoperative cerebral ischemia. In laparoscopic surgery, postural changes and pneumoperitoneum may further compromise ICA hemodynamics. This study aims to evaluate the effects of intraoperative postural transitions on ICA blood flow in patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery.MethodsA single-center, prospective, non-randomized observational study was performed.

pmc-12505761.title: Electric scooter related injuries among children: a single institutional experience
pmc-12505761.creator: Ali Abu-Kishk, Eran Kozer, Rony Beeri Berkowiz, Meital Ben-Ari, Ibrahim Abu-Kishk
pmc-12505761.description: BackgroundElectric scooter (ES) use has become increasingly popular, particularly among children. However, few studies have characterized pediatric ES-related injuries. We present our experience with children hospitalized due to ES-related trauma.MethodsA retrospective review was conducted of 103 pediatric patients hospitalized with ES-related injuries between 2018 and 2024.

pmc-12559412.title: The combined impact of fisheries and climate change on future carbon sequestration by oceanic macrofauna
pmc-12559412.creator: Gaël Mariani, Jérôme Guiet, Daniele Bianchi, Tim DeVries, Nicolas Barrier, Marc Troussellier, David Mouillot
pmc-12559412.description: Although the role of marine macrofauna in the ocean carbon cycle is increasingly understood, the cumulative impacts of fisheries and climate change on this pathway remain overlooked. Here, using a marine ecosystem model, we estimate that each degree of warming reduces macrofauna biomass and carbon export by 4.2% and 2.46%, respectively. Under a high emission scenario (SSP 5–8.

pmc-12647674.title: Sustainable gelatine–alginate biopolymer binder enhancing pigment printing and functional performance of textiles
pmc-12647674.creator: Nermin A Ibrahim, Heba M El-Hennawi, Safia A Mahmoud, Ahmed G Hassabo
pmc-12647674.description: This study investigates gelatine and sodium alginate as novel thickening agents for pigment textile printing using natural eco-friendly binders. As a thickener and binder, gelatine was tested in different ratios to sodium alginate. The study found that shear rate significantly affected gelatine gel-based thickener shear stress and viscosity. The study examined gelatine-based thickening agents’ elasticity and performance when thinned.

pmc-13462179.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). utinib, a once‐daily oral Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor, and venetoclax, a once‐daily oral B‐cell lymphoma 2 inhibitor, have both shown single‐agent activity in patients with relapsed/refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 Ibrutinib and venetoclax have complementary mechanisms of action, and the combination showed synergistic anti‐tumour activity in preclinical models of MCL 7 , 8 and high complete response (CR) rates in patients with relapsed/refractory MCL.

pmc-13602364.title: Paediatric Genetic Diseases: Models, Mechanisms and Therapies
pmc-13602364.creator: Kirsty Hooper
pmc-13602364.description: Summary: Disease Models & Mechanisms has launched a Special Issue focused on paediatric genetic disease. Here, we discuss recent research that highlights common themes and challenges in this area of research. Paediatric diseases – such as cancer, developmental disorders, metabolic disorders and neurodevelopmental disorders – can have strong genetic origins.

pmc-13612237.title: Periadrenal mature cystic teratoma mimicking adrenal myelolipoma: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-13612237.creator: Ran Hong
pmc-13612237.description: Mature teratomas arising in the adrenal region are rare and may mimic adrenal myelolipomas, particularly when adipose tissue is predominant. A 72-year-old woman with uncontrolled hypertension was found to have an 8.6-cm fat-containing mass in the right adrenal region, radiologically diagnosed as an adrenal myelolipoma. Laparoscopic adrenalectomy was performed.
